Analyses of Clinical Significance of the Changes for
the Complete Sample
As can be seen in Table 3, at postassessment the effect sizes in most
of the domains were in the moderate range, with the exception of the
SCL-90 and the PDI, which showed small to moderate effects and
negative symptoms for which no effect could be demonstrated.
The highest rates of reliable improvement were achieved for
positive symptoms (48%) and global functioning (56%). More
than two thirds of the patients (69%) showed reliable improvement
in at least one of the three PANSS scales. With regard to func-
tioning, improvement rates were largest in the domains work and
immediate social network. Rates of deterioration were generally
low and mostly ranged between 0% and 5%.

Figure 5B shows the relationship between the aggregate vari-
ability measure and FOA. Statistical tests showed a highly reliable
focus effect, p < .01 for the ANOVA and p < .001 for the linear
contrast, with greater variability for external FOA (see Table 1).
The ANOVA showed no significant effect of session (p = .26; see
Table 2) or session–focus interaction (p = .41,  2  .07). There-
fore there is strong support for the prediction of greater variability
of individual dimensions with external FOA.
